display_name: Soldatenarbeitszeitverordnung (Soldiers' Working Time Regulation), § 1 and Anlage, with Soldatengesetz § 30c and § 93(2): time off for soldiers' overtime, the exemption for international establishments, the power it rests on, and the citation requirement of Grundgesetz Art. 80(1) sentence 3
citation: Soldatenarbeitszeitverordnung vom 16. November 2015 (BGBl. I S. 1995), § 1 and Anlage as recast by Art. 5 No. 7 of the Verordnung vom 6. März 2025 (BGBl. 2025 I Nr. 78), in force 1 April 2025; Soldatengesetz §§ 30c, 30d, 93, as printed on gesetze-im-internet.de on 2026-11-02
authority: Federal Republic of Germany. SG § 93(2) no. 7 makes the Federal Ministry of Defence the maker of the regulations that disapply § 30c(1) to (3) and (5) under § 30c(6).

source.provider: gesetze-im-internet.de (Bundesamt für Justiz, run by juris GmbH); recht.bund.de (Bundesgesetzblatt)
source.note: Per-norm pages for SAZV § 1, its Anlage and Eingangsformel and SG §§ 30c, 30d, 93, converted to one line per paragraph; the gazette text of BGBl. 2025 I Nr. 78 (text and PDF). The previous annex (BGBl. 2022 I S. 1533) was not obtained.

why_this_subject: Felix Ringe and Linus Folkerts, 'Legal exploits may emerge at scale' (28 October 2026), https://www.felixringe.com/legal-exploits/, Case 3: they argue that the 2025 listing of NATO's Joint Support and Enabling Command (JSEC) in the Anlage is void because the amending regulation's preamble does not cite SG § 30c(6) with § 93(2) no. 7, the power to exempt soldiers at multinational establishments, so a soldier posted there keeps the time off for overtime that § 30c(2) gives. This subject encodes the entitlement, the exemption, the power and the citation test, and answers the soldier's question under both readings. It does not decide which is right.
encodings_note: One row. It encodes SG § 30c(2), (4) and (6), SG § 93(2) no. 7 and SAZV § 1 with its Anlage only, not the Soldiers Act or the Regulation; read the display_name as the subject, not as a claim about the encoding's coverage.
